categories.title: Domains & scan history
categories.lead: Choose whether the domain was the final page, the submitted URL, or a contacted resource.

templates.title: Recent primary-site observations
templates.note: Find recorded visits whose final page belongs to the selected domain or one of its subdomains.
templates.tip: Read the scan timestamp before treating a result as current.

templates.title: One exact primary hostname
templates.note: Match the complete final hostname, without including its subdomains.
templates.tip: Use the regular page.domain field when you want the whole domain tree.

templates.title: Originally submitted domain
templates.note: Find visits that started with the selected domain, even if navigation ended elsewhere.
templates.tip: Compare task.url with page.url to understand the destination.

templates.title: Domain contacted anywhere
templates.note: Find scans that contacted this domain as a page or resource.
templates.tip: A resource relationship alone does not identify the operator of a website.

templates.title: Subdomains without the apex
templates.query: page.domain:{domain} AND NOT page.domain.keyword:"{domain}" AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Look below the supplied domain while excluding that exact hostname.
templates.tip: Enter an apex such as example.com to explore its observed subdomains.

templates.title: Older primary-site observations
templates.note: Compare observations that predate your chosen lookback boundary.
templates.tip: Archive coverage depends on your account and does not prove continuous availability.

categories.title: Resources & connections
categories.lead: Trace what pages contacted and distinguish an embedded resource from the main site.

templates.title: Other sites contacting the domain
templates.query: domain:{domain} AND NOT page.domain:{domain} AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Find scans of other primary domains that requested something from the supplied domain.
templates.tip: Inspect the request list to identify the exact resource and initiator.

templates.title: Many contacted IP addresses
templates.note: Find observations with more than ten distinct contacted IP addresses.
templates.tip: CDNs, advertising and ordinary dependencies can all increase this count.

templates.title: Cross-country requests
templates.note: Review pages whose recorded requests reached IPs in multiple geolocated countries.
templates.tip: IP geolocation describes hosting observations, not the nationality of an operator.

templates.title: Busy request waterfalls
templates.note: Find scans with a large number of recorded resource requests.
templates.tip: Use the request waterfall to separate first-party code from third-party dependencies.

templates.title: Domain text in requested URLs
templates.note: Look for the domain text in any requested URL, including paths and query strings.
templates.tip: This is a text match; domain: is the better field for host relationships.

templates.title: Matching response content
templates.note: Find observations containing a response with the supplied SHA256.
templates.tip: The same library, stylesheet or image can legitimately appear on unrelated websites.

categories.title: Hosts & networks
categories.lead: Compare primary hosting with infrastructure contacted during a recorded page visit.

templates.title: Pages hosted on an IP
templates.note: Find scans whose primary page resolved to the supplied address.
templates.tip: Shared hosting and reverse proxies can serve unrelated domains.

templates.title: Any contact with an IP
templates.note: Find page observations that contacted the address anywhere in the request chain.
templates.tip: Open the requests to see whether the address served the page or a dependency.

templates.title: IP used as a secondary endpoint
templates.query: ip:{ip} AND NOT page.ip:{ip} AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Find scans that contacted the address while the primary page used another IP.
templates.tip: This narrows a pivot to secondary connections; it does not establish ownership.

templates.title: Primary hosting in an AS
templates.note: Find primary pages observed in the supplied autonomous system.
templates.tip: An AS usually covers infrastructure for many different customers.

templates.title: Connections to an AS
templates.note: Find any scan with a recorded connection to the supplied autonomous system.
templates.tip: Use page.asn when you only want primary hosting.

templates.title: AS used by dependencies
templates.query: asn:{asn} AND NOT page.asn:{asn} AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Find pages hosted elsewhere that contacted this AS.
templates.tip: Inspect resource URLs before drawing conclusions about a relationship.

categories.title: Redirects & responses
categories.lead: Follow the difference between a submitted address and the final page that the scanner saw.

templates.title: Submitted domain redirects off-site
templates.note: Find observations marked as redirecting away to another domain.
templates.tip: SSO, domain migrations and URL shorteners are common legitimate causes.

templates.title: Arrivals after off-domain redirects
templates.note: Find off-domain redirect observations that ended at the selected domain.
templates.tip: Inspect the original task.url and the recorded navigation chain.

templates.title: HTTP upgraded to HTTPS
templates.note: Find observations classified as an HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect.
templates.tip: The classification describes the stored navigation, not a new check.

templates.title: Successful primary responses
templates.note: Review observations where the final page returned HTTP 200.
templates.tip: A successful status code can still describe an error page rendered by the application.

templates.title: Missing primary pages
templates.note: Find stored visits with an HTTP 404 final response.
templates.tip: Use these records to compare old paths and migration behavior.

templates.title: Server-side error responses
templates.query: page.domain:{domain} AND page.status:(500 OR 502 OR 503 OR 504) AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Review recorded server and gateway failures.
templates.tip: A historical error is not evidence that the service is failing now.
templates.global_query: page.status:(500 OR 502 OR 503 OR 504) AND date:>now-{days}d

categories.title: Titles & file pivots
categories.lead: Use visible titles and known content hashes to find related observations.

templates.title: Phrase in a page title
templates.note: Search for a phrase in recorded page titles.
templates.tip: Matching titles are useful leads, not proof of a shared owner or malicious activity.

templates.title: Title phrase outside your domain
templates.query: page.title:"{title}" AND NOT page.domain:{domain} AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Find the title phrase on primary domains outside the supplied domain tree.
templates.tip: Review the screenshot and destination manually before classifying a lookalike.

templates.title: Exact complete page title
templates.note: Match the complete title field rather than a phrase within a longer title.
templates.tip: The search index lowercases text, so case is not an identity signal.

templates.title: Login-related titles in scope
templates.query: page.domain:{domain} AND page.title:(login OR "sign in") AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Locate observations with common authentication-page words in the title.
templates.tip: This is a label-based discovery aid and does not test authentication.

templates.title: HTML responses in scope
templates.note: Keep observations whose final response was classified as HTML.
templates.tip: MIME metadata is recorded from the scan and may not match the current response.

templates.title: Known downloaded file hash
templates.note: Look for the supplied SHA256 among files downloaded during scans.
templates.tip: Use hash: to search general HTTP response bodies instead.

categories.title: TLS & observation context
categories.lead: Read certificate and location fields as facts recorded at the time of a scan.

templates.title: Recently issued certificates
templates.query: page.domain:{domain} AND page.tlsAgeDays:[0 TO 7] AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Find scans where the observed certificate was no more than seven days old.
templates.tip: This age was measured during the scan, not today.

templates.title: Short certificate validity periods
templates.query: page.domain:{domain} AND page.tlsValidDays:[1 TO 30] AND date:>now-{days}d
templates.note: Find certificates recorded with total validity periods of one to thirty days.
templates.tip: tlsValidDays is the full validity duration, not the remaining lifetime.

templates.title: Certificates starting in the lookback
templates.note: Find observed certificates whose validity start falls in the chosen period.
templates.tip: Compare the scan time and certificate dates when reviewing renewal behavior.

templates.title: Primary hosting observed in Denmark
templates.note: Find scans with a primary hosting IP geolocated to Denmark.
templates.tip: A location filter does not identify where the website operator lives.

templates.title: Any Danish infrastructure contact
templates.note: Find scoped scans that contacted any IP geolocated to Denmark.
templates.tip: Use page.country to restrict the primary host rather than all requests.

templates.title: Large recorded response sets
templates.note: Find observations with more than ten million bytes of recorded subresource data.
templates.tip: Large pages, media and application bundles can all explain this size.

operators.description: Final page host and its domain tree.
operators.note: Includes subdomains.

operators.description: One complete final hostname.
operators.note: Use this for an exact hostname.

operators.description: Host in the URL originally submitted.
operators.note: Can differ from the final host after redirects.

operators.description: Host contacted anywhere during the visit.
operators.note: Includes resource requests and subdomains.

operators.description: Address used by the primary page.
operators.note: Shared infrastructure does not prove ownership.

operators.description: Address contacted by any recorded request.
operators.note: Network prefixes need an escaped slash, such as 203.0.113.0\/24.

operators.description: Primary hosting AS versus any contacted AS.
operators.note: Use the AS prefix.

operators.description: Primary IP country versus any contacted IP country.
operators.note: Use a two-letter country code.

operators.description: Time at which the scan was recorded.
operators.note: Not a publication date, first-seen guarantee or live status.

operators.description: Phrase or terms in the page title.
operators.note: Use page.title.keyword for the whole title.

operators.description: Recorded navigation classification.
operators.note: Other values include same-domain, sub-domain, parent-domain, sibling-domain and https-only.

operators.description: HTTP status of the final response.
operators.note: A server can use HTTP 200 for an application error.

operators.description: Primary response server header.
operators.note: The remote service controls its advertised header.

operators.description: Reported content type of the final response.
operators.note: Describes the stored scan.

operators.description: Text in any requested URL.
operators.note: A textual URL match is broader than a host match.

operators.description: HTTP response-body hash versus downloaded-file hash.
operators.note: Supply an observed SHA256; shared assets can match unrelated sites.

operators.description: Certificate age during the scan.
operators.note: This value is not recalculated as time passes.

operators.description: Full certificate validity duration.
operators.note: Does not mean days until expiry.

operators.description: Certificate validity start timestamp.
operators.note: Combine with a scan date window.

operators.description: Request count and distinct contacted IP count.
operators.note: Counts are context, not verdicts.

operators.description: Combine conditions and exclude matches.
operators.note: Use uppercase operators and parentheses.

operators.description: Inclusive numeric or date range.
operators.note: For a complete calendar month, an exclusive next-month boundary avoids ambiguity about the end timestamp.

operators.description: Pattern matching on supported fields.
operators.note: Leading wildcards and regular expressions require sign-in; regex is limited to supported RE fields.

operators.description: Outgoing links and rendered text.
operators.note: These are paid-plan fields: Professional, Enterprise or Ultimate. They are not used by the default templates.

patterns.title: Page or resource?
patterns.description: Start with the broad contact field, then exclude your own primary sites.
patterns.query: domain:example.com AND NOT page.domain:example.com AND date:>now-30d

patterns.title: Submitted here, ended elsewhere
patterns.description: Keep the original scope while excluding final pages in the same domain tree.
patterns.query: task.domain:example.com AND NOT page.domain:example.com AND date:>now-30d

patterns.title: Exact host, not its subdomains
patterns.description: The keyword field keeps the hostname match exact.

patterns.title: Title phrase on other domains
patterns.description: Look for title reuse and inspect each result before interpreting it.
patterns.query: page.title:"Example Organisation" AND NOT page.domain:example.com AND date:>now-30d

patterns.title: Secondary IP connections
patterns.description: Separate dependency requests from primary hosting.
patterns.query: ip:203.0.113.10 AND NOT page.ip:203.0.113.10 AND date:>now-30d

patterns.title: Group response conditions
patterns.description: Group alternatives before combining them with the domain scope.
patterns.query: page.domain:example.com AND page.status:(403 OR 404 OR 500) AND date:>now-30d

patterns.title: Review a precise time window
patterns.description: An inclusive start and exclusive end define the complete month.

patterns.title: Network prefix escaping
patterns.description: Escape the CIDR slash in an unquoted IP filter.

guide.title: Choose what the indicator means
guide.text: Use page.domain for a final website, task.domain for the submitted address, and domain for any contacted host. Apply the same primary-versus-any distinction to page.ip/ip and page.asn/asn.

guide.title: Bound the observation window
guide.text: Start with a recent lookback and widen it when needed. The date filter describes scan time. A missing result does not prove a domain was inactive, and an old result does not describe its current state.

guide.title: Build, then inspect the stored result
guide.text: Urlscanify opens a search of existing records. Review the result screenshot, navigation, request list and metadata on urlscan. It does not submit new scans or visit the investigated website for you.

guide.title: Keep relationships separate from attribution
guide.text: A shared IP, title or content hash can have ordinary explanations: CDNs, hosting, templates and common libraries. Follow the specific request or redirect before deciding what a relationship means.

guide.title: Know the account boundaries
guide.text: Search visibility, quotas and historical coverage depend on your urlscan account. Leading wildcards and regex require sign-in. Rendered text, outgoing links and verdict fields are restricted to the documented paid plans.

guide.title: Preserve the evidence context
guide.text: Record the result link, scan timestamp and query used. Keep assessment notes and exports in your own controlled storage. Opening a query sends its terms to urlscan; this UI does not store service credentials.
